reasons: Each rule has a matching test, and failures name the rule that broke.
Phrase checks are a limited filter, not a guarantee.

terms.meaning: a Python tool that finds and runs tests
a shared setup function that tests can request, so the same sample data is not repeated
a fake stand-in for the AI model that returns scripted answers, so tests run without calling the real service
the agreed shape of a piece of data, such as which fields it must have
the set of nine scored dimensions a process receives

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File setup and imports
sections.what: Imports the assessor, its output shape, the scorecard types, the model tier settings, and shared fixtures. Also builds the list of dimension names from the scorecard.
sections.why: Tests loop over every dimension the scorecard defines, so the list is built once from the schema.
sections.watch_out: Dimension names come from the scorecard model, so renaming one changes many tests.

sections.name: anyio_backend
sections.title: Async test engine selection
sections.what: Selects asyncio as the engine that runs the async tests in this file.
sections.why: Likely reason: async tests need a runner, and this file fixes it to asyncio.

sections.name: current_state
sections.title: Sample current state
sections.what: Builds one sample process description with a single manual spreadsheet step and no pain points or workflow debt.
sections.why: Reason not stated beyond use as shared test input.

sections.name: output
sections.title: Fake model answer
sections.what: Builds a stand-in model answer where every dimension scores three. Tests can pass in custom rationale text for chosen dimensions, and nature-of-work values are fixed.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets tests run the assessor without calling the real model, and lets rationale text be varied.
sections.watch_out: The default rationale wording is used by checks, so changing it can change results.

sections.name: TestHappyPath
sections.title: Happy path checks
sections.what: Checks the assessor returns a scorecard and nature-of-work values, sends the request to the standard model tier, and includes the current state text in the message to the model.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the test names.

sections.name: TestTheInversionIsStated
sections.title: Inverted dimensions flagged in task
sections.what: Checks the two dimensions where a high score is bad, fragmentation and change burden, are named in the task text. Also checks the task says five is worse and warns against ranking the hardest processes as the best opportunities.
sections.why: The docstring says a model shown similar fields may score them all in the same direction.
sections.watch_out: Adding a new inverted dimension requires updating the task text, or these checks fail.

sections.name: TestBoundary
sections.title: Assessor cannot emit recommendations
sections.what: Checks the output has no derived score, posture, future state, steps or agents fields. Recommendation or ranking language in a rationale is refused, while a plain rationale passes.
sections.why: Reason stated in the test names: the assessor scores and does not redesign or price.
sections.watch_out: The phrase match is a limited filter, so a reworded recommendation may get through.

sections.name: TestFailurePaths
sections.title: Failure path checks
sections.what: Checks a score above five cannot be built. Checks a citation to evidence not in the pack is rejected with the id named. Also checks an assessment with no evidence still produces a scorecard, with empty citations.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the test names.

summary: A set of tests that checks the process assessor scores the nine dimensions, and does not redesign or price the process.
purpose: Proves the assessor returns a scorecard and nature-of-work values, refuses recommendations and derived scores in its written rationale, and refuses citations to evidence it was not given.
why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the file's one-line docstring. The assessor's output is used later, so wrong scores would spread.
how: Pytest loads the file. Shared fixtures build a sample current state and a fake model answer. Each test runs the assessor against the fake answer and checks one rule, such as the routed model tier, a rejected rationale, or a refused citation.
inputs: A fake model client returning scripted answers, a sample current state, the process brief from the shared test fixtures, and a run context.
outputs: Pass or fail results for each test. Nothing is written to disk.
risks: The boundary checks match phrases, so a reworded recommendation could pass. The tests use a fake model, so they do not show how the real model behaves.
debug: If a test fails, read the error message first. Check the assessor module and its task text for the rule named. If a test mentions a dimension, check the scorecard model for the dimension list.
